evidence: STATIC DESIGN (no structural inversion found): (1) Harness is template-identical: diff of task tests/scoring.toml, tests/test.sh, tests/tools/score.py vs rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/* reports no differences. scoring.toml:1-11 gates render=0.0/constraints=0.0, weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2, floors functional=0.05. score.py:40-48 reward = weighted mean only if every gate > 0.0 and functional > 0.05, else 0.0 -- each term is non-decreasing in every dimension score, so an app that is at least as good on every criterion can never receive a lower reward from the formula. (2) Gates are all_pass binary criteria (gates/render/judge.toml:14-24, gates/constraints/judge.toml:14-24) that test a minimal subset of public behaviour (sign-in refusal/acceptance; Recruiter opens job + adds candidate, Observer in independent context sees it) -- a stronger conforming app has no way to fail them that a weaker one passes; neither gate demands a hidden requirement (Observer reads all per hireops_rules.md:18). (3) Mass: functional 43 binary criteria, weight sum 58.5 (computed), max single-criterion share 2.5/58.5=4.3% of functional (2.6% of reward); polish 5 binary (sum 12) and visual 5 likert (sum 6) together cap at 0.4 < functional 0.6, and the 0.05 floor plus 'Likert 1 normalizes to zero' (visual prompt gate paragraph) stop a dead-but-pretty app farming 0.4. (4) Dead features cannot earn refusal credit: functional prompt.md:13 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control: a successful action of the same kind, observed in this review'; criteria name explicit controls (e.g. hro_mgr_early_refused 'their late-stage moves are the control', hro_undo_once 'The successful undos are the control', hro_bulk_places 'the later two-card move ... succeeds as the control'); hro_candidate_no_staff/hro_candidate_private 'A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'; polish hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0'. prompt.md:17 forbids counting a stale/version refusal as a rule refusal, closing the 'refuse everything as conflict' exploit. (5) Setup dependency inversion is mitigated: prompt.md:13 'When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job ... never earns credit', and protocol T falls back to Tomas's seeded conversation if hro_candidate_linked fails. (6) Requirements behind high-weight strict rows are public (401: hireops_rules.md:21; focus on refused card: hireops_rules.md:85; 30-per-page: :144-145; seen/observer: :164-166; per-person drafts: instruction.md:7), so a conforming app is not penalised for an unstated convention. TRIED: broken app that could pass -- server that refuses every mutation with 409 'changed': blocked by prompt.md:17 and per-row controls; app accepting all invalid actions passes hro_activity_refusals (w0.5) vacuously but loses ~15 refusal rows, net far lower. Conforming alternative that could fail -- app returning 403 instead of 401 to anonymous fails hro_anonymous (w1.5), but 401 is public (hireops_rules.md:21), so not an inversion. RESIDUAL NON-MONOTONE RISKS (measurement, not design): (a) judge budget: functional prompt.md:53 converts an exhausted budget into binary 0 'NOT EXERCISED'; a fully working app forces every protocol (S..D, many replays, 15 s waits) to run inside functional judge timeout 9000 s (functional/judge.toml:4) and suite budget 11100 s (test.sh:224), whereas a weak app fails fast -- a stronger app could therefore lose late rows (A activity, D restart) to budget exhaustion that a weaker app never reaches. No full configured timing measurement exists. (b) Judge stochasticity on 43 conjunctive binary rows. (c) hro_activity rewards an app with fewer successful actions slightly (fewer lines to log) -- bounded at weight 1 and dominated by the lost feature rows. MISSING EVIDENCE: raw-evidence-index.json scope states verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' Its only runtime artifacts are scripted golden observations (workspace.cjs/results/*, hash a424b50f... verified), which do not score any app through rewardkit. REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Runtime and model evidence' requires a hash-bound reward-ordering record (e.g. golden vs mutated weak apps through the full configured verifier); none exists. Per SKILL 'Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass', the ranking claim stays Not exercised with risk=true, although static analysis found no design defect.
suggested_fix: No design change needed; produce a hash-bound reward-ordering record: run the full configured verifier (rewardkit + configured judge) on the golden and at least two graded-down mutants (e.g. no live updates; no undo; refuse-everything-as-stale) and confirm reward(golden) > reward(partial) > reward(broken), recording functional judge wall time against the 9000 s budget.
